notes: Tooling fix — no register proposals (bundle claims: []). T536 fixes the keeper re-firing pre-claim deaths. THE INCIDENT (measured 2026-08-20 12:00Z, incoming Orchestrator boot): the Ollama account hit its session usage limit; every glm-5.2:cloud launch died in ~22s with a 429. The keeper dispatched 80 times into that wall in ~3.5 min (T511×57, T517×14, T512×3, plus one each of T513/T515/T516/T518/T519/T520) before being stopped by hand. ROOT CAUSE: bin/dispatch is fire-and-forget (detached Popen, prints 'dispatched …' and returns immediately — bin/dispatch:294-305) and the row only becomes in_progress when the worker runs managent claim. A worker that dies before claiming leaves the store unchanged, so the keeper's next iteration recomputed an identical world and re-fired the same row. T504's heal-cooldown could not catch it: both its signals (a fresh heal record, and claim_count>=2) require the worker to have claimed. THE FIX, three layers in tools/fleet-keeper.sh: (1) dispatch-attempt memory — every firing is persisted to untracked/fleet-keeper.attempts.json ({task, model, ts, pid}); a row fired within FLEET_DISPATCH_COOLDOWN (default 300s) is not eligible, whatever the store says, and a row whose recorded pid is still alive is never double-fired; (2) per-row consecutive-failure backoff — an attempt is failed when, on a later iteration, its recorded pid is gone AND the row never left dispatchable; consecutive failures back off exponentially 300→600→1200, cap 3600s, reset on a real claim (which fully clears the per-row record, last_ts included); the park reason is logged in one line; (3) per-model circuit breaker — FLEET_MODEL_FAILURE_TRIP (default 3) distinct rows dying pre-claim on one model benches that model: LANE-DOWN logged, untracked/fleet-keeper.lane-down.json written, model_allowed() and least_data_model() refuse the benched model, re-probed once per FLEET_LANE_RETRY (default 1800s). The one-writer invariant and the cooldown dead-man's switch are unchanged — the row adds refusal reasons, it never adds a dispatch. TEST-FIRST (red demonstrated): the five controls were added to tools/regression-fleet-keeper.sh (a seeded stub_die.py that exits non-zero without claiming, plus attempts/lane-down seeding helpers and wait_dead/attempt_pid/attempt_failures), and the two seeded arms were run against the PRE-FIX keeper and observed RED — T536-1 showed T1 re-fired every iteration (O2 = 'dispatched T1' instead of 'none') and T536-2 showed T1 fired 4× instead of T1,T2,T3-then-none, the exact incident signature. After the fix, sh tools/regression-fleet-keeper.sh reports ALL CONTROLS PASSED (exit 0), including the three null controls (a healthy claim brakes nothing; an expired backoff window re-dispatches; an expired lane re-probes). The harness is already wired into zig build test (build.zig:497 test_step.dependOn). D036 AMEND (read and acked via bin/managent inbox T536 --ack; the operator's directive, relayed via claude-fable-5): (1) DURABLE DENYLIST — shipped FLEET_MODEL_DENY=glm-5.2,minimax-m3,kimi-k2.7 as a documented DEFAULT in the script (DEFAULT_DENY in the python), chosen over a separate committed config file because it is the single self-documenting source, lives next to the other env knobs, and is exactly the 'documented default in the script with the reason and the review date' form the operator named acceptable; the comment carries the reason (Ollama weekly quota exhausted) and the REVIEW instruction (restore the empty default when the quota clears). Semantics: an UNSET FLEET_MODEL_DENY now applies the durable default; an explicitly-set value — even the empty string — overrides it, so the regression suite (which must allow glm-5.2) now sets FLEET_MODEL_DENY='' instead of unsetting it, and arm T536-6 asserts the unset→default-deny behaviour (glm refused, deepseek-v4-flash dispatched). (2) RESTART — the keeper was stopped (pid 91635 gone) and the cooldown flag was present; per the directive I cleared the flag (tools/fleet-cooldown.sh off) and started exactly one keeper (nohup bash tools/fleet-keeper.sh, now pid 47334; confirmed via pgrep that no second keeper runs). FLEET_MODEL_DENY is UNSET in the keeper's process environment, so the durable default is in force. The live log then read 'at cap (5/5)… at cap (6/5) — no dispatch' — the fleet was already at/over cap with real in_progress deepseek-v4-pro workers (T537-T540 + this T536), so no live dispatch was observable to confirm the at-most-once behaviour directly; the absence of any 'dispatched' spam is itself the confirmation that the incident signature is gone, and the at-most-once-per-row guarantee is proven deterministically by regression arm T536-1. (3) RUNNING-SCRIPT-REWRITE HAZARD — noted: bash reads a script incrementally, so restarting a live loop mid-rewrite can execute a half-written file. This DOES deserve its own row: a keeper that execs a snapshot of itself (e.g. reads the file fully into a shell variable before the loop, or a start wrapper that copies the script to a temp file and execs that) would make restart-during-edit safe. (4) pgrep FALSE-POSITIVE (finding for T511, not fixed here) — a naive single-instance guard `pgrep -f fleet-keeper` false-positives on ANY worker whose brief/command line mentions the file (measured at boot: pgrep -f fleet-keeper returned 2 while zero keepers ran, matching the T536 and T514 worker command lines). T511 owns the single-instance guard and must not ship `pgrep -f fleet-keeper`; it needs a narrower match (exact script path) or a pidfile/lockfile.
